name: Federalism
summary: Federalism holds that political authority should be divided between a central government and regional governments, each with powers the other cannot simply take away, usually set out in a written constitution. Adherents argue this restrains tyranny, lets diverse communities govern themselves, and keeps a large state together. It is a structural doctrine and has no fixed position on economic or social policy.
scope: Mainstream constitutional federalism as described in Wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, drawing on Madison and Hamilton (Federalist Nos. 39 and 51), Montesquieu, Althusius and Mill. Covers both coming-together (US, Switzerland) and holding-together (India, Belgium) federations. Excludes anarchist federalism (Proudhon), and the specific US Federalist Party and states-rights politics. Because it is a form of government, most policy answers are neutral and low confidence.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Guaranteed regional self-rule with its own laws is the core of federal design, and asymmetric arrangements that let one region keep distinct institutions are an accepted federal variant.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Federalist No. 39 grounds legitimate government in the people and rules out hereditary or divine authority, and federal constitutions are secular instruments of limited power.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Federalism is a structural doctrine with no position on tax design; adherents hold varied views.

character-from-environment.rationale: A question of moral psychology that federalism does not address.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Federalist No. 51 and the whole design of divided and checked power aim to bind rulers by constitutional limits, so an unbound sovereign contradicts the doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Unrelated to the division of powers; adherents hold varied views.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Federalist No. 39 describes the American constitution as a compound of national and federal elements, and its checks and balances echo mixed government, though this is inferred rather than the doctrine's own claim.

leader-cult.rationale: Federalist No. 51 assumes rulers are not angels and need checking, so public glorification of a leader is inferred to be foreign to the doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: A family-law question outside the doctrine's scope; adherents differ.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Structural doctrine; inferred from its concern with limited, divided power rather than class conflict.

land-redistribution.rationale: Structural doctrine with no position on land policy; federations differ.

refugee-return.rationale: Structural doctrine with no position on refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional division of powers within settled borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from its constitutional-liberal tradition; it takes no direct stance on religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Structural doctrine; inferred from its liberal-constitutional tradition.

common-currency.rationale: Federations differ on currency union; adherents are split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Structural doctrine; no position on kin unions across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Federalism is described as letting diverse communities self-govern within one state, including holding-together federations for national minorities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from its aim of accommodating minorities within a shared state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Structural doctrine; Federalist authors argue from institutions and ambition, not economic forces.

ban-cartels.rationale: Structural doctrine with no position on competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Structural doctrine with no position on bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Federalist No. 51 and the written-constitution model rest on checks that limit majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Structural doctrine with no position on gender quotas.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Federalist No. 39 grounds republican government in the people rather than hereditary power.

elective-rulers.rationale: Federal systems exist as both republics and monarchies (for example Canada and Belgium), so the doctrine does not settle how rulers are chosen.

minority-veto.rationale: Federal constitutions protect regions and minorities through amendment thresholds and divided powers, not through a veto for any single dissenter, which is inferred from the checks described in Federalist No. 51.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Federalism exists to restrain tyranny through constitutional limits, so adherents would accept resistance to a ruler who breaks them; the right of resistance itself is inferred, not stated.

parliament-supreme.rationale: A federal constitution divides and entrenches powers, so no legislature, parliament included, can be supreme over the constitution and the regional governments.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Federalism values diversity but is itself offered as a widely applicable design, so it does not settle this.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Constitutional federalism places force under civil constitutional authority, so a political guardian role for the army is inferred to be rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: The doctrine does not address this; adherents take varied positions, so it is left neutral.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Federalism is silent on family policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from subsidiarity and regional self-government: lower levels of government can set rules that fit local conditions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Federalism is silent on employment policy; adherents take varied positions.

democratic-peace.rationale: Federalism does not address this claim; adherents are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Federalism rests on constitutional law and consent, so adherents lean against a view that denies any general duty of obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Federalism is about internal divisions of power and is silent on outside intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation is outside the doctrine.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Madison argues that a divided, checked system protects minorities, and the doctrine rejects hostile claims about groups.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Federalism is silent on marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the checks-and-accountability case for limited government, which favours open government.

local-production.rationale: Subsidiarity favours local decisions but not necessarily local production; adherents are split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Federalism is built on permanent constitutional institutions and levels of government, which sits against purely informal organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Adherents are split: US-style federalists stress constitutional supremacy, while European federalists favour supranational law.

religious-nation.rationale: Federalism is meant to hold diverse communities together, so defining the nation by one religion cuts against it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Federalism concerns internal division of power and is silent on relations between states; its adherents take varied positions.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Doctrine is silent on fiscal sharing; federal systems differ between equalisation and regional retention, and adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Federalism is a structural doctrine and silent on property; adherents take varied positions.

defeat-communism.rationale: Federalism is silent on foreign and ideological conflict; adherents take varied positions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Federalism is silent on how services are delivered; adherents take varied positions.

religion-illusion.rationale: Federalism is silent on religion; adherents take varied positions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Federalism is silent on economic history; adherents take varied positions.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Federalism is silent on gender and economics; adherents take varied positions.

socialized-care.rationale: Federalism is silent on domestic and care work; adherents take varied positions.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Federalism is silent on language policy; federations often protect regional languages, but adherents differ on a national language.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from federalism's principle that powers and agreements entrenched in a constitution cannot be changed unilaterally by one level of government.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Federalism keeps a constitutional order of divided governments rather than replacing it with communal societies.

majority-settlement.rationale: Federalism protects regional self-rule, including of minority-majority regions, so state-steered majority settlement cuts against its principles.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Federalism is silent on economic systems; adherents take varied positions.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Federalism concerns the division of power, not rival land claims; it can serve claims of either kind.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Federalism is a form of government and silent on the matter; adherents as committed to constitutional order and evidence would reject denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Federalism lets sub-units decide such matters, and adherents take varied positions.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Madison's Federalist 51 grounds the division of power in checking tyranny and protecting minorities, which suppressing opposition would undermine.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Federalism leaves religion to the constitution's division of powers; adherents differ.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Madison's Federalist 39 rests government on the consent of the people; inferred as against rule for the ruler's benefit, though federalism does not address colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Federalism is silent on religious duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Federalist 39 grounds authority on consent of the governed, not on religious law, but federalism as a doctrine takes no position on this; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The SEP cites self-government at regional and local levels as a justification for federalism, close to citizens taking part in decisions; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Federalism is a structural doctrine and silent on social theory.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Federalism lets states or regions decide such rights, and federal adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Federalism allows sub-units to differ on such questions, and adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Federalism concerns the structure of government and is compatible with any political side.

alienated-labor.rationale: Federalism is silent on economic theory.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Federalism is silent on religions or culture.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Federalist 39 states that the government derives its powers from the people, not from God, though federalism as a doctrine does not address it directly.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Federalism lets regions decide such rules, so adherents are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Federalism is silent on employment law, which may be set at either level.

social-market-economy.rationale: Fiscal federalism is compatible with many economic systems and the doctrine takes no view.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Federal states keep armed forces and defence is a central function, though the doctrine does not require it; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Foreign alignment is outside the doctrine.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Federalism concerns dividing power between levels of government and is silent on succession; federations include monarchies such as Belgium and Canada, so adherents split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A structural doctrine with no position on banking; inferred as neutral.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Federalism is silent on this; adherents hold varied views on international lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: The Federalist papers ground authority in the people and their representatives through a broad franchise, though they left franchise rules to the states; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: A structural doctrine with no position on gender or ecology; inferred as neutral.

reification.rationale: Federalism says nothing on capitalism's social relations; adherents could take any view.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Federalism does not address press ownership; Madison's concern is checks on power among government institutions, so inferred as neutral.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Federalist No. 51 and constitutional federalism rest on written constitutions and law that binds rulers, so rule by standing law is consistent with it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Federalism divides power by territory not race, and No. 39 grounds government in the people at large; inferred opposed, since the doctrine is not about group exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed, as the internet postdates the doctrine; a structural doctrine with no position on participation technology.

open-government-data.rationale: Federalism is silent on records and openness; Madison argued for checks on power in general, but the topic was not discussed directly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Federalism is about territorial divisions of power and says nothing on religion; federal constitutions generally protect religious liberty, so inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Federalism is silent on this; its aim of keeping diverse communities in one polity (see s1) points against group boycotts, but this is inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Federalism concerns dividing power between levels of government and is silent on sortition; Madison favoured representation, but adherents vary and some federations use citizens' assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Federalism is a constitutional form that takes no position on religious doctrine, and its adherents vary widely.

missingStatements.text: A national constitution should divide power between central and regional governments, each with powers the other cannot remove.
missingStatements.rationale: Constitutionally entrenched division of sovereignty is the defining feature of federal systems.

notes: Anarchist federalists and EU-style supranational federalists would answer several statements differently. Many answers are neutral because federalism is a form of government compatible with left and right policy.
